luis (Customer): Hey, after upgrading to the v2 tagged release of the Go SDK I'm getting 401s when fetching via `go get` from our CI. Works locally for me though.

amanda (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste the exact `go get` output and your go.mod?

luis (Customer): Sure, here's the relevant bits:
```
$ go get github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go@v2.0.1
go: downloading github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go v2.0.1
go: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go@v2.0.1: reading github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go/go.mod at revision v2.0.1: 401 Unauthorized
```
and my go.mod line is `module github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go` (no /v2 suffix)

felix (Go SDK): hm that's the classic v2 module path mismatch. For a v2 tagged release the module path inside go.mod must include `/v2` (semver+Go modules). If it doesn't, proxies can mix things up.

raj (Eng): Also possible GOPROXY/GOPRIVATE interaction. If the repo is private or we're replacing to a private path, an unauthenticated proxy can return 401. Are you using any `replace` directives?

luis (Customer): Yes there's a `replace github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go => ../local-redwood` in our module for testing, but CI doesn't have that. We also set `GOPRIVATE=github.com/redwood-inference` in CI env.

amanda (Support): Quick checklist: (1) confirm module path in the library's go.mod, (2) ensure tag matches semver v2.x.y, (3) verify GOPRIVATE and auth creds in CI, (4) try `go clean -modcache` and `GOSUMDB=off` to isolate proxy behavior.

felix (Go SDK): If the published tag v2.0.1 has go.mod with `module github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go` then `go` will expect import path without /v2 for previous major version. Since the tag has v2 it becomes inconsistent -> proxies often fetch the tag and then fail when go requests v2 metadata. Workaround: add `/v2` to module path in go.mod and cut a new tag, or use an import path with `/v2` explicitly: `require github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go/v2 v2.0.1` in consumers.

luis (Customer): Is there any quick workaround so our CI isn't blocked? We can't cut a release right now.

raj (Eng): Two options: (A) use a `replace` in your project's go.mod pointing to a commit sha on the remote repo via `replace github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go/v2 => github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go v0.0.0-20240225123456-abcdef123456` (pointing to pseudo-version) — that forces the path. (B) set GOPROXY direct to bypass caching: `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct` or `GOPROXY=direct` (if you have auth to Git).

sre-bot: Note: CI service logs indicate multiple failed `go list` HTTP requests returning 401 from internal git hosting at 2024-11-05T14:12:03Z.

amanda (Support): Felix — can Eng confirm whether the tagged release on our repo has the module path fixed? If not, we should cut a patch and push guidance.

felix (Go SDK): I'll check the repo now. Quick grep shows v2 tag was pushed but go.mod wasn't updated (module path missing `/v2`). That's the root cause.

felix (Go SDK): Proposed fix: update go.mod to `module github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go/v2`, bump to v2.0.2, tag and push. Also add a note in the release notes about `/v2` break.

amanda (Support): Amanda to coordinate release and send customer temporary workaround. Luis — for immediate unblock, try adding this to your project's go.mod:
```
replace github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go/v2 => github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go v0.0.0-20240225123456-abcdef123456
```
then run `go get` again. If your CI can't access the git host, use `GOPRIVATE` + proper SSH key or token.

luis (Customer): OK will try that and report back. Thanks.

raj (Eng): After the next tagged fix we'll also publish a short KB entry on v2 module path pitfalls and CI proxy symptoms (401 at `reading ... go.mod at revision`).

felix (Go SDK): Created internal ticket INF-GO-412 to cut v2.0.2 and update docs. ETA 24h.

amanda (Support): Closing loop once Luis confirms. If still blocked we can ship a small patch branch and point CI at it. :thumbsup:

luis (Customer): Workaround worked — CI pulled the pseudo-version replace and `go build` succeeded. Thanks everyone! :rocket!
